geometry_edits.rationale: Retarget the dominant bend to the long plan axis so the mass reads as one continuous neighborhood bar rather than a shallow lateral kink.
Reduce the bend slightly to keep the primary gesture calm and capacity-bearing while improving sectional continuity.
Increase subdivision so the bend can resolve more smoothly across views and reinforce a continuous dominant mass.
Keep the threshold notch aligned to the access side so the visible public response remains semantically correct.
Slightly enlarge the entry cut to strengthen ground-level public legibility without breaking the overall compact datum.

rationale: The candidate is a coherent early massing with a readable dominant bent-slab idea and a protected notch that at least suggests an access-side public threshold. It fits neighborhood_living reasonably well because it can support compact mixed-use/ground-active occupation, but the void is still modest and the section is fairly generic, so the program relation is only partial rather than exemplary. The silhouette is continuous and not fragmented across views, and there is no visible collision problem. Compared with the references, it resonates most with the compact carved-datum lineage, but it lacks the stronger court/public-open-space consequence and clearer active ground edge shown in the best precedents. The main correction would be to deepen the carved public void or make the access response more legible while preserving the dominant bent mass.
